problem.text: In the accompanying figure, the outer square $S$ has side length $40$. A second square $S'$ of side length $15$ is constructed inside $S$ with the same center as $S$ and with sides parallel to those of $S$. From each midpoint of a side of $S$, segments are drawn to the two closest vertices of $S'$. The result is a four-pointed starlike figure inscribed in $S$. The star figure is cut out and then folded to form a pyramid with base $S'$. Find the volume of this pyramid.

steps.title: Where to start: the star is a net of the pyramid
steps.body: The problem says the star is folded into a pyramid with base $S'$. So $S'$ is the base, and each of the four triangles becomes a slanted face. The volume of a pyramid is $\tfrac{1}{3}\cdot(\text{base area})\cdot(\text{height})$, so we need the base area and the height.

your_turn.prompt: What is the area of the base $S'$?

steps.title: Read the slant height off the flat star
steps.body: Each triangle is isosceles, and its height from its base (a side of $S'$) up to its tip is the slant height $s$ of the pyramid. Walk straight across $S$ through the center: you cross one triangle's height, then $S'$, then the opposite triangle's height, from one side of $S$ to the other. So $$s + 15 + s = 40.$$

steps.title: Find the right triangle inside the pyramid
steps.body: After folding, the tip of the pyramid sits straight above the center of $S'$. The slant height runs from the tip down to the midpoint of a side of $S'$. So there is a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the slant height $12.5$, whose vertical leg is the height $h$, and whose flat leg goes from the center of $S'$ to the midpoint of one of its sides. Careful: that flat leg is half the side of $S'$, not half its diagonal (the half-diagonal goes with the slanted edge, not the slant height).

your_turn.prompt: How long is the flat leg, from the center of $S'$ to the midpoint of one of its sides?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: By the Pythagorean theorem, $7.5^2 + h^2 = 12.5^2$, so $h^2 = 156.25 - 56.25 = 100$ and $h = 10$. The volume is $$\tfrac{1}{3}\cdot 225\cdot 10 = 750.$$ The answer is **$750$**.
